about.card1.body: An engine that resolves fresh editions every day, for every channel, for every surface a partner runs. A house of art directions we can tune or rebuild per brand. And a production process that gates every edition before it ships. The AI does the volume. Writers and showrunners decide what is good. Neither half works alone and we are not interested in pretending otherwise.
about.card1.head: What we built
about.card2.body: Over twenty writers, showrunners, game designers and AI engineers out of film, television and games. We move fast, we ship on schedule, and we hold a prestige bar on subject matter that most of this category does not bother with.
about.card2.head: Who is in the room
about.card3.body: Daily games became some of the most valuable attention a brand or a publisher can own, while much of the industry was still calling them a nice-to-have. The gap is not creative and it is not technical. Daily games are a standing production line, and almost nobody can run one, let alone several. We can, and we would rather run them under your brand than compete with you for the same audience.
about.card3.head: Why now
about.hero.h1: We make the thing you can’t staff.
about.intro.body: Wolf Games is the game studio inside Wolf Entertainment, the company behind Law & Order. Procedural television is the discipline of making self-contained stories on a schedule, at a quality bar that does not move, for years at a time. A vault of daily games is the same job on a tighter clock across several channels at once.
about.join.body: We are hiring writers, designers and engineers, and we are talking to partners about pilots.

hiw.axes.label: How an edition gets specific
hiw.axes.sub: The same story skeleton is filled three ways, out of your world, for every channel. The result is editions that could only have been written for your audience, where the specific detail does the plot work rather than sitting on top as decoration.

hiw.chan.label: The vault, not a title
hiw.chan.sub: A channel is one game with one continuing story and its own host, and someone subscribes to the channel rather than to the site. The vault holds a set of them, so a person who bounces off one mechanic still finds one that fits. Every channel runs the same daily pipeline out of the same source material.
hiw.close.body: The demo is the real build, running the same bundle and the same start sequence a partner embed uses. Switch the world underneath it and watch the edition change.

One integration carries the whole vault, and adding a channel later needs nothing from your engineers. We host and operate all of it. No SDK, no app store, nothing to maintain on your side.

legal.c2.body: Play events: what was started, what was finished, how long it took, what was answered. No account is required and none is offered in a pilot.
legal.c2.head: What we collect
legal.c3.body1: Play events answer one question: is this working, for this audience, this week. That signal is shared between your team and ours, and it compounds. Every edition that runs teaches the next one what your audience actually finishes, so the vault gets sharper for them specifically. Play telemetry never enriches a third-party profile, is never sold, and is never joined to an advertising identity graph.
legal.c3.body2: The event log is the source of truth for both of us. You read the same events we read, which is the only way a retention number survives your own scrutiny.

pain.1.obs: Bought attention does not compound. Every campaign starts the audience from zero again.
pain.2.obs: A few seconds of passive view time is what most paid placements return, and it is the number under the most pressure internally.
pain.3.obs: The IP already performs. What is missing is a reason to open it on a Tuesday when nothing has launched.
pain.4.obs: Licensed catalog games are available, cheap, and instantly recognizable as somebody else’s product with a logo on it.
pain.5.obs: There is appetite for something like this at the top of the house, and no appetite for a two-year build to find out.

stance.bet.1: Our bet is that serialized stories with daily drops and hosts worth returning to bring someone back the next day without a push notification.

stance.expect.2: We expect a game built out of your world to pull harder than a licensed catalog identical on a hundred other surfaces.
stance.expect.3: We expect a set of channels to hold a broader share of your audience than any single mechanic can.

stance.proven.2: One line of code puts the whole vault in front of your audience. We host it, run it, and refresh the content.
